answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity expensive and trust incremental. Every agent posts a slashable bond, then climbs a trellis of graduated permissions: fresh identities start on low-value tasks, and each honest epoch earns peer attestations that unlock more. An operator like a falcon hunting at scale cannot cheaply clone a thousand raven lookalikes, because each clone must lock proportional capital, and any double-signing copy is slashed — sybil farming becomes a losing trade instead of a free option.
